nodes.summary: P1 functions are continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of P1 functions

nodes.summary: Nodal vectors with zero boundary values `d₀ = dₙ = 0`.
nodes.title: Nodal vectors with zero boundary values

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of the stiffness matrix: `dᵀ K c = ∑ᵢ (cᵢ₊₁ - cᵢ)(dᵢ₊₁ - dᵢ) / hᵢ`.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the stiffness matrix

nodes.summary: The slope `(dᵢ₊₁ - dᵢ) / hᵢ` on the `i`-th element of the P1 function with nodal values `d`.
nodes.title: Slope of a P1 function on a mesh element

nodes.summary: The `i`-th element vector `eᵢ = δ_{i+1} - δᵢ` of the assembly.
nodes.title: Element vector of the stiffness assembly

nodes.summary: The weak form for `C¹` test functions vanishing at `0` and `1`: `∫₀¹ u' v' = ∫₀¹ f v`.
nodes.title: Weak form of the classical solution for $C^1$ test functions

nodes.summary: The weak form for P1 test functions: `∫₀¹ u' v_h' = ∫₀¹ f v_h`.
nodes.title: Weak form of the classical solution for P1 test functions

nodes.summary: The stiffness matrix is the Gram matrix of the hat functions: `a(φⱼ, φₖ) = Kⱼₖ`.
nodes.title: Stiffness matrix is the Gram matrix of the hat functions

nodes.summary: The energy form of two P1 functions: `a(p1 c, p1 d) = ∑ᵢ (cᵢ₊₁ - cᵢ)(dᵢ₊₁ - dᵢ) / hᵢ`.
nodes.title: Energy form of two P1 functions

nodes.summary: The key identity of the 1D P1 method: for `w` continuous on each element, differentiable inside it, and with integrable derivative there, `a(w, p1 d) = ∑ᵢ slopeᵢ(d) (w(xᵢ₊₁) - w(xᵢ))`.
nodes.title: Energy pairing with a P1 function via nodal differences

nodes.summary: `‖u - u_h‖_a² ≤ (h / π)² ‖f‖²_{L²(0,1)}`, so the energy error is `O(h)`.
nodes.title: Energy error estimate

nodes.summary: Best approximation (Céa's lemma for the symmetric energy form, with constant `1`): `‖u - u_h‖_a ≤ ‖u - v_h‖_a` for every `v_h ∈ V_h`.
nodes.title: Best approximation

nodes.summary: `‖u - I_h u‖_a² ≤ (h / π)² ‖u''‖²_{L²(0,1)}`, with `h` the mesh size.
nodes.title: Interpolation estimate

nodes.summary: Element-wise form of the energy of `u - p1 d` for a `C²` function `u`: `a(u - p1 d, u - p1 d) = ∑ᵢ ∫_{xᵢ}^{xᵢ₊₁} (u' - slopeᵢ(d))²`.
nodes.title: Element-wise energy of a function minus a P1 function

nodes.summary: The energy form `a(u, v) = ∫₀¹ u'(x) v'(x) dx` of `-u'' = f`. For a P1 function, `deriv` is junk at the mesh nodes, a null set.
nodes.title: Energy form of the equation $-u'' = f$

nodes.summary: Endpoint equality, derived from the open-interval equation by continuity of `-u''` and `f`: the two sides agree on `(0, 1)`, hence on its closure `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Classical solutions satisfy the equation on the closed interval

nodes.summary: `a(u - u_h, v_h) = 0` for every `v_h ∈ V_h`.
nodes.title: Galerkin orthogonality

nodes.summary: Inside an element, `p1 P d` has derivative `slopeᵢ`.
nodes.title: Derivative of a P1 function inside an element

nodes.summary: The hat function of an interior node lies in the P1 space.
nodes.title: Interior hat functions lie in the P1 space

nodes.summary: The hat function `φⱼ` of node `j`: the P1 function equal to `1` at `xⱼ` and `0` at every other node.
nodes.title: Hat function of a mesh node

nodes.summary: The element estimate: a `C²` function vanishing at `a` and `b` satisfies `∫ₐᵇ (g')² ≤ ((b - a) / π)² ∫ₐᵇ (g'')²`.
nodes.title: Element estimate for $C^2$ functions vanishing at both ends

nodes.summary: An integral over `[0, 1]` is the sum of the integrals over the elements.
nodes.title: Integral over the unit interval as a sum over elements

nodes.summary: Wirtinger's inequality on `[a, b]`: a `C¹` function vanishing at `a` and `b` satisfies `∫ₐᵇ g² ≤ ((b - a) / π)² ∫ₐᵇ (g')²`.
nodes.title: Wirtinger's inequality on an interval

nodes.summary: `‖u - u_h‖²_{L²(0,1)} ≤ (h / π)⁴ ‖f‖²_{L²(0,1)}`, so the `L²` error is `O(h²)`. The proof uses nodal exactness and Wirtinger's inequality on each element, not the Aubin–Nitsche duality argument.
nodes.title: `L²` error estimate

nodes.summary: The nodal interpolant `I_h u`: the P1 function with nodal values `u(xⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Nodal interpolant of a function

nodes.summary: `u` is a classical solution of `-u'' = f` on `(0, 1)` with `u(0) = u(1) = 0`. We ask `u` to be `C²` on all of `ℝ`, which is no loss for the interval problem (a `C²` function on `[0, 1]` extends), and `f` to be continuous. The equation is stated on the open interval, as in the Dirichlet problem: requiring it at the endpoints without regularity of `f` would be a genuine strengthening. With `f` continuous, endpoint…
nodes.title: Classical solution of the Dirichlet problem $-u'' = f$

nodes.summary: The nodal values of the exact solution solve the Galerkin system.
nodes.title: Nodal values of the exact solution solve the Galerkin system

nodes.summary: The Galerkin system has at most one solution (`K` is positive definite on nodal vectors with zero boundary values).
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the Galerkin solution

nodes.summary: The coefficient vector `c` solves the Galerkin system: zero boundary values and `(K c)ⱼ = Fⱼ` at every interior node `j`. The Galerkin solution is `u_h = p1 P c`.
nodes.title: Solution of the Galerkin system

nodes.summary: The load vector `Fⱼ = ∫₀¹ f φⱼ`.
nodes.title: Load vector of the P1 method

nodes.summary: Membership in the P1 space: `v = p1 P d` for nodal values `d` with `d₀ = dₙ = 0`.
nodes.title: Characterization of membership in the P1 space

nodes.summary: In one dimension the P1 Galerkin solution is the nodal interpolant of the exact solution: `u_h = I_h u`.
nodes.title: In one dimension the Galerkin solution is the nodal interpolant

nodes.summary: On the `i`-th element, `p1 P d` is the linear function through `(xᵢ, dᵢ)` with slope `slopeᵢ = elementSlope P d i`.
nodes.title: P1 functions are linear on each element

nodes.summary: `p1` as a linear map from nodal values to functions.
nodes.title: Linear map from nodal values to P1 functions

nodes.summary: `p1 P d` interpolates the nodal values.
nodes.title: P1 functions interpolate their nodal values

nodes.summary: The P1 finite element space `V_h` with zero boundary values: the image under `p1Map` of the nodal vectors vanishing at both ends.
nodes.title: P1 finite element space with zero boundary values

nodes.summary: The continuous piecewise linear (P1) function with nodal values `d`: `d₀ + ∑ᵢ slopeᵢ · rampᵢ(x)`. On `[0, 1]` it is linear on each element and takes the value `dⱼ` at `xⱼ`; outside `[0, 1]` it is constant.
nodes.title: Continuous piecewise linear function with given nodal values

nodes.summary: The clamped ramp of the `i`-th element: `0` left of `xᵢ`, `x - xᵢ` on `[xᵢ, xᵢ₊₁]`, and `hᵢ` right of `xᵢ₊₁`.
nodes.title: Clamped ramp function of a mesh element

nodes.summary: The energy error estimate in norm form: `‖u - u_h‖_a ≤ (h / π) ‖f‖_{L²(0,1)}`.
nodes.title: Energy error estimate for the P1 Galerkin solution

nodes.summary: The off-diagonal entry of an element: `K_{i, i+1} = -1 / hᵢ`.
nodes.title: Off-diagonal stiffness entry of an element

nodes.summary: Entries between nodes two or more apart vanish (tridiagonality).
nodes.title: Tridiagonality of the stiffness matrix

nodes.summary: The diagonal entry at an interior node `xⱼ` shared by consecutive elements `i` and `j`: `K = 1 / hᵢ + 1 / hⱼ`.
nodes.title: Diagonal stiffness entry at an interior node

nodes.summary: The assembled stiffness matrix `K = ∑ᵢ (1 / hᵢ) eᵢ eᵢᵀ` on all nodes: each element contributes `(1 / hᵢ) [[1, -1], [-1, 1]]` at nodes `i, i + 1`.
nodes.title: Assembled stiffness matrix of the P1 method

nodes.summary: Every element length is at most the mesh size `h`.
nodes.title: Element lengths are bounded by the mesh size

nodes.summary: Every element has positive length.
nodes.title: Mesh elements have positive length

nodes.summary: The length `hᵢ = xᵢ₊₁ - xᵢ` of the `i`-th element of the mesh.
nodes.title: Length of a mesh element

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
